Real payload added Week 7 Batch 5 (docs/DECISIONS.md item 104). Schema: type (matches smuggling_configs.json's "type"), raw_request_template (a raw HTTP/1.1 request with {method}/{path}/{host} format placeholders, sent byte-for-byte, base64-encoded, as services/smuggling_engine/smuggling.go's wire contract's raw_request_b64 field). The Content-Length/chunked-encoding mismatch in each template is the probe itself, not a bug -- a correctly-framed request would never produce the timing differential this scanner looks for. Exact byte sequences are PortSwigger's own published timing-technique examples (https://portswigger.net/web-security/request-smuggling/finding, "Finding CL.TE/TE.CL vulnerabilities using timing techniques"), verified against that source before being stored here, not invented: CL.TE's body is exactly 7 bytes ("1
A
X") against a declared Content-Length of 4 (the front-end forwards only "1
A", a chunk-size line plus 1 byte of chunk data with no terminating CRLF -- the back-end, parsing chunked encoding, then waits for the CRLF that never arrives). TE.CL's body is exactly 6 bytes ("0

X") against a declared Content-Length of 6 (the front-end, parsing chunked encoding, treats the leading "0

" as a complete, already-terminated chunked body -- a 0-length chunk always ends chunked framing -- and forwards only those 4 bytes; the back-end, parsing Content-Length, then waits for the 2 bytes that were never sent).

payloads.raw_request_template:
POST {path} HTTP/1.1
Host: {host}
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Length: 4

1
A
X

POST {path} HTTP/1.1
Host: {host}
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Length: 6

0

X
